name: King of Sidon
overview: The King of Sidon was a male ruler who reigned during the time of King Zedekiah of Judah, as mentioned in Jeremiah 27:3. Beyond his kingship and the period in which he lived, Scripture provides no additional personal details or tribal affiliations. His role as a king places him among the regional leaders interacting with Judah during a critical historical era.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Sidon' straightforwardly identifies this person as the monarch of the city of Sidon. The name means 'king [of] Sidon' and is a descriptive title rather than a personal name, reflecting his political office rather than a given name from God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or personal connections for the King of Sidon beyond his identification as a ruler during Zedekiah's reign. No further relational details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Sidon holds significance as a contemporary ruler during the reign of Zedekiah, situating him within the geopolitical context addressed by the prophet Jeremiah. His mention underscores the broader network of kings and nations involved in the events surrounding Judah's history at that time. Although details are sparse, his inclusion in Jeremiah 27:3 highlights the interconnectedness of regional powers under divine sovereignty.
